content:
There are several comments ahead that says that this tool is useless for squaring the gantry. That's true, because that isn't what it's supposed to do.
It's used to align the gantry in Z-direction.

So be careful to not bend the gantry out of square when using it, and after the alignment is done, check the squareness by pushing the gantry against the front stop. Note that you don't have to release the screws if it's just a little bit out of square. You can straighten it anyway.

Despite others saying to skip im going to try and do this step anyway so i can try to figure out why it actually exists.

wish me luck :)

if anyone at prusa is reading this, i would suggest giving some diagrams of the intent behind certain steps like this. if i could visualize what the goal actually is then it would be easier to determine the importance of the step and possibly assist with improving the procedure

replies.content: Came back to say it was a success. i have the second version of the parts with the 3rd screw access cutout. also i chose to slide the tools all the way to the front so they were touching the frame stop. youll see in the next few steps and ill comment there too.

content:
!!! STOP HERE !!!

As usual, the comments section knows what's up.

Doing the next part will likely throw your gantry out of alignment. The Aligner Tools have 3-5cm of slop in them once installed, and after following all the instructions my gantry was indeed out-of-square.

If your gantry is already square with successful prints, skip this section. If you need to square it, there are many instructions online on how to use the front stop-blocks as a guide. You WILL have better success with that method than using these tools.
There is a new revision of this tool (E2/R2) with enough room to screw all 3 screws without removing the tool.
I skipped gantry alignment since I had a working core one. My build is complete and it's printing fine. This alignment is not necessary if your Core One is printing fine before the upgrade.

replies.content: Read the comments on the next few steps. Redoing gantry alignment on a working printer can actually cause issues, especially since the gantry aligner tools don't have clearance for the third/lowest screw on each side of the gantry.
